page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.3xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine hosted on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 6 physical cores and 12 virtual CPUs with dedicated CPU allocation and hyperthreading enabled. It is equipped with 48 GB of memory, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4 GB per core. Hardware cache specifications include 32 KB of L1d cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache per socket. The instance does not include local NVMe SSD storage or dedicated GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage while delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight moderate multi-threaded capability alongside restrained single-core throughput. Single-core processing metrics, such as a stress-ng score of 1109.09 and a Geekbench single-core score of 950.0, place in the lower quartile, accompanied by lower single-threaded Gzip compression performance. In contrast, multi-core execution scales efficiently to average levels, demonstrated by a multi-core stress-ng score of 8832.77 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4757.0. The server handles concurrent processing steadily, recording 8.86 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark CPU score of 10094.6. LLM inference processing achieves 653.12 prompt tokens per second on small 135M parameter models, though performance decreases significantly on medium 7B models.

The ecs.g5.3xlarge presents a balanced resource ratio for general cloud infrastructure demands. Its cost efficiency stems from providing substantial memory capacity alongside 12 dedicated vCPUs without the added expense of hardware accelerators or bundled local SSD storage. The trade-off involves lower single-threaded clock speed efficiency, making it less optimal for latency-sensitive single-threaded jobs. This hardware configuration is best suited for general application servers, middle-tier web backends, multi-threaded background task processing, software compilation, and moderate database workloads.
